out.rationale: Amodei et al. ask how to ensure an agent respects aspects of an objective too expensive to evaluate often during training. Christiano et al. propose Iterated Amplification, which builds a training signal for problems too complicated for a human to evaluate by combining solutions to easier subproblems, and present results in algorithmic environments. There, amplification needed tens of thousands of examples to learn the decompositions, while supervised learning needed tens of millions, which they say would be a prohibitive cost if an external expert provided the examples.

text: The authors propose Iterated Amplification, a training strategy that progressively builds up a training signal for problems too complicated for a human to evaluate directly by combining solutions to easier subproblems. They describe it as closely related to Expert Iteration but using no external reward function, and present results in algorithmic environments showing it can efficiently learn complex behaviors.
title: Iterated Amplification: training signal built by combining solutions to easier subproblems
